summary: High-fidelity quantum non-demolition (QND) multi-qubit Pauli $Z$ measurements provide a practical alternative to bias-preserving CNOT gates for fault-tolerant computation with phase-flip-dominant noise, working universally across all qubit platforms including two-dimensional systems. Circuit-level simulations show that asymmetric XZZX surface codes with weight-four QND $Z$ measurements achieve a phase-flip threshold of $\sim\!1.25\%$ and up to $6\times$ qubit overhead reduction compared to bias-unaware codes at $\eta = 10^4$, while repetition codes reach $\sim\!2.3\%$ threshold with overhead comparable to bias-preserving CNOT schemes.
motivation: Noise bias—where phase-flip errors dominate bit-flips—enables hardware-efficient fault-tolerance, but existing approaches require bias-preserving CNOT gates that are experimentally challenging and provably impossible for strictly two-dimensional qubits.
method: We demonstrate that QND multi-$Z$ measurements can replace bias-preserving CNOT gates for compiling all operations in bias-tailored error correction. We propose physical implementations using nuclear spins coupled to electron spin ancillas (via hyperfine interaction and spin-to-charge readout) and dissipatively stabilized superconducting cat qubits (via engineered three-wave mixing on asymmetrically threaded SQUIDs), and numerically evaluate asymmetric XZZX surface codes and repetition codes under circuit-level biased noise.
result: At $\eta = 10^4$, XZZX + $M_{Z^4}$ achieves phase-flip threshold $\sim\!1.25\%$ with $6\times$ overhead reduction; repetition code with QND $Z$ measurements reaches threshold $\sim\!2.3\%$ with overhead matching bias-preserving CNOT schemes, eliminating the need for such gates.
